title: Topic Routing Payload
description: Maps a student topic to the office that owns it, the queue an escalation goes to, and whether the KB can answer it at all. This content exists on no web page -- it is institutional knowledge that has to be authored, and it is what turns a contact list into a working front desk.

topic.description: Canonical name for the thing the student needs.

aliases.description: How students actually say it. Official office names are rarely what anyone searches for.

office.description: Owning office. Should match a contact record's display_name.

office_contact_id.description: id of the contact record supplying live phone/email, so the number lives in one place.

kb_coverage.description: answerable = the KB has what's needed. partial = general answer possible, specifics need the office. route-only = hand off immediately, no attempt. never-answer = Tier 3; the handoff IS the correct answer and no content may be added later.

topic_data_tier.description: Sensitivity of the TOPIC, not of this record. The routing record itself is always Tier 0 public information -- 'mental health support is handled by Counseling Services' is not confidential, and it is precisely the record that guarantees a human handoff exists. Do not conflate the two: a topic_data_tier of 3 must pair with kb_coverage 'never-answer', which the validation gate enforces.

requires_own_record_lookup.description: True when answering needs the student's own data (a hold, a balance, an award). Out of scope until Phase 3, so these route today even where content exists.

answer_guidance.description: What the bot may say before handing off. Kept short and specific.

handoff_needs.description: What to collect from the student so the office doesn't have to ask. Populates the escalation card.

urgency.description: crisis bypasses normal routing entirely and follows the crisis protocol.
